D: A swinging sixties secret agent is thawed out in 1997 to stop his old enemy Dr. Evil.
P: Serve the snacks when Austin is unfrozen in the nineties.
S: Classic devilled eggs piped with a creamy mustard yolk filling, dusted with smoked paprika and topped with crisp bacon crumbs and chives. Lower 8 eggs into boiling water and cook 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel. Halve lengthways and scoop out the yolks. Mash the yolks with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp white vinegar and salt until smooth. Pipe or spoon back into the whites. Grill 3 rashers bacon until crisp and crumble finely. Dust the eggs with smoked paprika and top with bacon and snipped chives.

Cubes of sharp cheddar, fresh pineapple, cocktail onions and cabana on toothpicks, stuck into half a rockmelon like a retro party hedgehog. Cut half a rockmelon in two and place one quarter cut-side down on a platter as the hedgehog body, with two cloves pushed in for eyes. Cut 250g vintage cheddar and half a fresh pineapple into 2cm cubes. Slice 150g cabana into rounds. Thread toothpicks with a cube of cheese, a cube of pineapple and either a cocktail onion or a slice of cabana. Push them all over the rockmelon until it is covered in spikes.
M: Dr. Evil's one million dollar steak Diane
Dr. Evil's one million dollar demand

Thin sirloin steaks flashed in a hot pan with a creamy mushroom, brandy and Dijon sauce, served with crisp shoestring fries and watercress. Bake 1kg frozen shoestring fries at 220C for 20 minutes. Bat out 4 sirloin steaks to 1cm thick, season and sear in a very hot pan with oil for 90 seconds a side. Rest on a plate. In the same pan, melt 30g butter and fry 200g sliced mushrooms and 1 diced shallot for 3 minutes. Add 40ml brandy and let it bubble off, then add 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp Dijon and 150ml cream and simmer 2 minutes. Pour over the steaks and serve with fries and watercress.
W: Sherry-soaked jam sponge layered with thick vanilla custard, raspberries and whipped cream, topped with a Union Jack of strawberries and blueberries. Slice a 300g jam rollette into rounds and line a large glass bowl. Drizzle with 60ml sweet sherry. Scatter over 200g raspberries. Pour over 600ml thick vanilla custard and chill 1 hour. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar to soft peaks and spread over the top. Lay halved strawberries in a cross and diagonals across the cream, then fill the gaps with 125g blueberries to make a Union Jack.
K: An ice-cold dry gin martini stirred with a splash of dry vermouth, strained into chilled glasses and finished with a lemon twist or olive. Chill 4 martini glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Fill a large jug with ice, add 240ml gin and 40ml dry vermouth, and stir steadily for 30 seconds until very cold. Strain into the chilled glasses. Peel 4 thin strips of lemon zest, twist each over a glass to spray the oils and drop it in, or add a green olive on a pick for those who like it briny.
